title: nehogy + -jon/-jen: So That Something Doesn't Happen

sections.title: The negative purpose clause
sections.content: nehogy is nem + hogy fused into one word, and it flips a purpose clause negative: instead of aiming for something to happen, you're acting to PREVENT it. Korán indulok, nehogy elkéssek a megbeszélésről means "I'm leaving early so that I'm not late for the meeting" — the verb stays in -jon/-jen exactly as before, nehogy alone carries the negative meaning, so don't add nem as well.

sections.title: nehogy + -jon/-jen
rows: so that I'm not late for the train
so that I don't forget the plan
so that the obstacle doesn't hold me back

items.spanish: Kétszer ellenőrzöm a jegyzeteimet, nehogy hibázzak a vizsgán.
items.english: I check my notes twice so that I don't make a mistake on the exam.

items.spanish: Alaposan megtervezem a napomat, nehogy elveszítsem az időmet.
items.english: I plan my day carefully so that I don't waste my time.

sections.content: nehogy already contains the negative — Nehogy elfelejtsem never adds nem (Nehogy ne felejtsem el would double-negate and mean something like "so that I don't not forget", not what you want). If you need a positive purpose clause instead, drop the ne- and go back to plain azért, hogy.
